claims.text: The initial nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst is a solid solution.
The initial catalyst has a homogeneous, random atomic distribution.
Mild annealing below 300°C can controllably and uniformly increase lattice strain in the catalyst.
The proposed mild annealing can increase strain without causing phase segregation, significant sintering, or substantial nanoparticle growth.
Lattice strain perturbs local interatomic spacings in the catalyst.
Increased lattice strain shifts the d-band center of surface metal atoms.
A strain-induced d-band-center shift changes the adsorption energies of ethanol and its reaction intermediates.
The adsorption-energy changes optimize intermediate binding and make ethanol oxidation proceed more efficiently.
The proposed electronic and adsorption changes reduce catalyst poisoning.
Relative to the unannealed catalyst, the annealed catalyst will have a lower ethanol-oxidation onset potential.
Relative to the unannealed catalyst, the annealed catalyst will produce higher ethanol-oxidation current densities.
The annealed catalyst will have improved selectivity toward desired ethanol-oxidation products.
The predicted effects apply in acidic electrolyte near room temperature.
The predicted effects apply only while annealing avoids phase separation, extensive sintering, and substantial particle growth.
The exact d-band-center shift and its quantitative kinetic effect are uncertain.
Absence of a statistically significant d-band-center shift or absence of improved electrochemical performance relative to the unannealed control would falsify the hypothesis.
